summary.oneLiner: One of India's leading electrical and electronics (E&E) companies, among the top two players in wiring harnesses for two-wheelers and three-wheelers in India with a leadership position in EV 2W/3W wiring harnesses.
summary.business: Dhoot Transmission designs, engineers, manufactures and supplies critical wiring harnesses that integrate electronic sensors and controllers, switches, terminals, connectors, junction boxes, high-voltage interconnection systems and data cables, for both ICE and EV platforms. Its product lines are wiring harnesses, battery packs, sensors and electronic controllers, and automotive switches, sold mainly to 2W and 3W OEMs in India with a diversified presence extending into commercial vehicles, off-highway vehicles, and farming/industrial equipment.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward integrated in critical wiring-harness components — terminals, connectors, cables and moulded parts — manufactured in-house to lower procurement overhead, secure supply against external disruption, and enable in-line quality control. Principal raw materials are copper, brass and polymers plus connectors, terminals, cables, mouldings (incl. rubber) and electronic components (sensors, PCBs); sourced domestically (principally Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Haryana) and internationally (China, Switzerland, Germany). All suppliers are required to be IATF-certified. Company strategy also includes forward moves into power electronics/charging sub-systems (DC-DC converters, on-board chargers, BJB sub-systems) and expansion of EV battery-pack interconnect systems from a single- to a multi-customer model.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- Established leadership position in India's 2W/3W wiring harness market: 44.64% value share in 2W+3W combined (Top 2), more than 70% share in electric 2W/3W (Leader), FY2025 (Source: CRISIL Report)
- Backward integration in critical components (terminals, connectors, cables, moulded parts) lowers costs, secures supply and improves quality control
- Marquee, diversified OEM customer base with long-standing relationships (average relationship with top five customers of 13 years as of Dec-2025); top 5 customers combined 2W market share of 66.24% of the Indian 2W market

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- 66.91% of FY2025 revenue from operations came from the 2W automotive sector and 12.50% from 3W, with wiring harnesses alone comprising 78.00% of FY2025 revenue - any downturn in 2W/3W demand or wiring-harness pricing/technology directly hits the business
- Top customer Bajaj Auto contributed 35.08% of FY2025 revenue (32.33% in 9M Dec-2025); top 5 customers contributed 71.18% of FY2025 revenue (72.49% in 9M Dec-2025) and top 10 customers 81.81% - loss of any major OEM relationship would be materially adverse
- Hosur (wiring harness) and Chakan, Pune (battery pack assembly) facilities are under construction with expected completion in Q2 and Q1 FY2027 respectively (per Risk Factors); company flags possible delays/cost overruns from regulatory approvals and construction delays
- 26 tax proceedings pending against the Company and 2 against Subsidiaries as of the UDRHP-I date, with aggregate amount involved of approx Rs.234 million (Company) and Rs.2.81 million (Subsidiaries); materiality threshold for civil litigation is Rs.136.09 million
- Company was unable to locate certain historical RoC records (Form 18/challan for a 2007 registered-office change) and relied on an independent search report; DRHP also flags an instance of certain non-compliances under the Companies Act in the past
- Net debt to EBITDA rose to 1.51x (9M Dec-2025) from 0.99x (FY2024), while net capex ran at 11.17% of revenue in FY2025, as the company funds new plants partly through debt
- BC Asia XV (Bain Capital) acquired a 49% stake in April 2025 (now 55% pre-Offer) and the Company completed a common-control acquisition of Dhoot Holdings Private Limited and downstream entities during 9M ended Dec-2025, requiring restatement of FY2023-FY2025 financials as if combined from April 1, 2022

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Setting up the Jhajjar Wiring Harness Plant (Haryana) funded from IPO Net Proceeds, with commissioning by May 2027.**
- **Setting up the Hosur Wiring Harness Plant (Tamil Nadu) funded from IPO Net Proceeds; Objects-of-Offer schedule targets commissioning around May 2027, while the Risk Factors section separately describes this facility as expected to complete …**
- **Battery pack assembly facility under construction at Chakan, Pune, expected to complete by Q1 FY2027.**
- **Plan to establish a state-of-the-art R&D/testing centre with integrated design, engineering, advanced testing and validation capabilities, funded through internal accruals and sanctioned term loans; no cost or completion date disclosed.**
- **Scale EV battery pack interconnect capabilities from a single-customer model to a multi-customer model to broaden addressable market and share of wallet.**
- **Expand into high-voltage power electronics and charging sub-systems - initial roadmap includes DC-DC converters, on-board chargers and BJB sub-systems, targeting the commercial vehicle segment.**
- **Pursue selective acquisitions, joint ventures and technology partnerships in Europe and Asia to gain new technologies, customers and markets, including the DASPL-Ride Vision Limited ADAS joint venture (DASPL 67% / RVL 33%) under a master …**
- **Utilise Net Proceeds to repay/prepay outstanding borrowings of Subsidiaries DACPL, DESPL, DASPL and Dhoot Transmission UK Limited.**
- **Continue increasing overall capacity utilisation as new plants ramp, building on a rise from 57.81% (FY2023) to 64.22% (FY2024) to 75.40% (9M ended Dec-2025).**
- **Apply a measured capital allocation and governance framework with Board-level oversight, product/geographic diversification matrix and defined ROCE targets when evaluating acquisitions; no numeric ROCE target disclosed.**
